memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Abraham's servant heard what they said, he bowed down to the ground before the LORD. Then the servant brought out gold and silver jewelry and articles of clothing and gave them to Rebekah; he also gave costly gifts to her brother and to her mother." - Gen 24:52-53 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Again the servant bows down and worships. This is the second time in the chapter he stops to praise God, and it reveals a heart tuned to gratitude. Every time the Lord answers, his instinct is to worship. Thanksgiving had become his habit, not just his emergency response.

Only after worship does he bring out the gifts. There is an order here worth noticing: God first, then generosity. His joy in God overflowed into blessing others. The costly gifts to Rebekah and her family were expressions of a heart already full of gratitude to the Lord.

A thankful heart naturally becomes a generous heart. When we truly grasp how much God has given us, holding tightly to our own things feels smaller and smaller. The servant's open hands flowed from his bowed head.

Take a moment to check the rhythm of your own life. Do you pause to worship when God answers, or do you rush on to the next thing? And does your gratitude to God spill over into kindness toward people? Let worship come first, and let generosity follow as its natural fruit.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is thanksgiving my habit or only my emergency response?
2. Does my gratitude to God overflow into generosity toward others?
3. Do I pause to worship when God answers my prayers?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, make worship my first response and generosity its natural fruit. Fill my heart with gratitude that overflows into blessing others. Amen.
